question: Can a pre-outcome trade-network path state identify which adaptation outcome family follows a concentration-and-flow stress event, out of sample, better than persistence and target-history baselines?
hypothesis: Trade stress is followed by distinguishable path families—stable replacement, diversification, fragmentation, or failure-to-adapt—and the path-state rule improves out-of-sample multiclass prediction without requiring a single partner identity or a causal claim.
causal_scope: No causal claim. The event is an observed endogenous network transition; causal validation is out of scope for this contract.

source.input_policy: Use existing official XG observation aggregate or tracked shards only; no new acquisition, imputation, missing-as-zero, source averaging, or frequency conversion.

universe.reporters: The 135 reporters with fixed ten-partner pools inherited from IMF IMTS V2 selection register.
universe.candidate_pool: The fixed ten counterpart identities per reporter; partial annual observation is allowed and its observed_count is recorded.
universe.partial_coverage_policy: A state is valid only when at least five of ten candidates have positive numeric observed values. Missing candidates remain missing and do not enter observed_total or shares.

state_schema.derived_share_policy: Shares are descriptive ratios computed from observed raw values within the fixed candidate pool; they are not replacements for raw values and are not used to alter raw data.
state_schema.flow_stress: observed_total_raw_usd at t <= 0.70 times the lower of observed_total_raw_usd at t-1 and t-2
state_schema.concentration_stress: top1_share at t <= top1_share at t-1 minus 0.10
state_schema.top1_exit: top1_identity at t differs from top1_identity at t-1

event_definition.definition: A valid event occurs when t-1 is high concentration, t-2 and t-1 are valid states, t is valid, and at least one of flow_stress, concentration_stress, or top1_exit is true.
event_definition.information_set: Only states through t are used to classify the event; outcomes begin at t+1.
event_definition.overlap_policy: Use the first qualifying event per reporter in each rolling-origin training/evaluation window; do not use overlapping outcome windows within a reporter.

path_candidate.rule: If top1_exit and the new top1 share at t >= 0.40, predict stable_replacement; else if concentration_stress, predict diversification; else if flow_stress, predict failure_to_adapt; otherwise predict fragmentation.
path_candidate.probability_policy: Fit-only multiclass probabilities are estimated by outcome frequency conditional on the candidate path subtype; if a subtype has no fit support, use fit-wide family prevalence and record fallback.
path_candidate.complexity: Four deterministic branches, no post-confirmation threshold search.

outcome_families.classification_time: At t+h using valid states from t+1 through t+h.
outcome_families.stable_replacement: The top1 identity at t differs from t-1 and remains the same top1 identity at every valid year t+1 through t+h.
outcome_families.diversification: At t+h, top1 share is at least 0.10 below t-1 top1 share and top1 share is >0.50.
outcome_families.fragmentation: At t+h, top1 share <=0.50 and stable_replacement is false.
outcome_families.failure_to_adapt: None of the preceding families applies while all required future states are valid.
outcome_families.unclassifiable: Any missing required future state; excluded from that horizon, never imputed.

evaluation.training_rule: For origin o, use events whose event year <= o; evaluate events in (o, o+2] with required future horizon available. No later event enters training.
evaluation.primary_metric: Multiclass Brier score at h=2 on the locked final block, candidate minus each baseline; lower is better.

baselines.state_persistence: Fit-only most frequent outcome family conditional on event subtype flags (high concentration, flow stress, concentration stress, top1 exit).
baselines.target_history: Fit-only overall outcome-family prevalence by horizon.
baselines.previous_state: Fit-only one-step state-transition baseline: most frequent outcome family conditional on pre-event concentration bucket and top1-exit flag.

null_controls.method: Permute contiguous blocks of annual state records within reporter, with fixed block lengths 2 or 3; recompute events, candidate predictions, and outcomes.
null_controls.purpose: Tests whether path performance exceeds local temporal continuity alone.

null_controls.method: Assign placebo event years from valid non-event years within reporter while preserving event count, pre-event gap, and future-horizon eligibility; recompute path outcomes.
null_controls.purpose: Tests whether the path works at actual stress timing rather than arbitrary valid years.

null_controls.method: Within reporter-year, randomly reassign the observed candidate identities to the observed raw values; preserve observed_count, observed_total_raw_usd, rank multiset, and valid-year mask; recompute all states and outcomes.
null_controls.purpose: Tests whether adaptation-family prediction depends on observed partner identity structure rather than aggregate volume and rank shape.

multiple_testing.primary_family: Candidate versus three baselines at h=2 on the final locked block.
multiple_testing.correction: Holm-Bonferroni alpha=0.025 for the three primary baseline comparisons.
multiple_testing.secondary_family: Other horizons, rolling origins, and family-level metrics reported with Benjamini-Hochberg q=0.025; no secondary result can promote the candidate alone.

admission.primary_brier: Candidate Brier at h=2 is at least 0.05 lower than every baseline after the primary family correction.
admission.accuracy: Candidate macro-F1 and exact family accuracy are not lower than every baseline and improve over the best baseline by at least 0.05 in the final block.
admission.rolling_stability: Candidate Brier improvement versus the best baseline is non-negative at all four rolling origins and at least 0.02 at three of four origins.
admission.family_coverage: At least 30 final-block events and at least 10 events per scored outcome family; otherwise not_testable.
admission.nulls: All three nulls are non-degenerate and the primary candidate advantage passes Holm-adjusted alpha.
admission.concentration: No reporter contributes >5% of final-block events; influential top-three fit reporters are excluded and primary direction remains positive.
